accuracy.evidence: Facts checked against named sources: malaria deaths about 608,000 in 2022 (WHO World Malaria Report 2023, shown as 'about 600,000'); unprovoked fatal shark bites 10 worldwide in 2023 and a 2013–2022 average near 6 (ISAF, Florida Museum; shown as 'under 15 a year'); 93% of US students rated their driving above the median (Svenson, 1981); Weinstein (1980) unrealistic optimism; £10 today vs £11 tomorrow preference reversal (Thaler, 1981); teens' risk-taking rising with peers present in a driving game, adults barely changing (Gardner & Steinberg, 2005); risk vs uncertainty (Knight, 1921); availability heuristic (Tversky & Kahneman, 1973); groupthink symptoms (Janis, 1972). Arithmetic: 26/52 red cards, median splits 30 as 15/15, raffle and counter chances, s − n/2 gap.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented errors: treating uncertain choices as if odds were known (sort step and 'known' tag), 'vivid = common' (prediction 'sharks', availability step), assuming consistent time preferences (prediction 'yes: the wait is one day both times'), 'most of us can be above average' (prediction '28' / 'all 30'), believing awareness of a bias removes it (m5), and that a group being sure means it is safe (groupthink step).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrisk models this topic's mechanisms: a risk/uncertainty card sort, a 'feels likely' bar that grows with each news story while the real-death bars do not move, the Thaler now/later preference-reversal pair, a draggable middle line across 30 ranked drivers with 28 ringed self-ratings, a group chat about jumping off a pier where groupthink signs are flagged, and a six-step decision plan to order. flagbias is about assumptions about people; the distinct gate passed under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each bias is felt before it is named: three stories push the pink bar up but the real numbers then show mosquitoes far ahead; the learner's own choices in A and B are played back ('You switched…'); the line only balances at 15 below / 15 above, with 28 ringed, so the impossibility is visible; tapping Jay's tide question gives 'a real question about the facts breaks groupthink'; the plan rejects 'Choose' before options and facts.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: 'sharks' for which kills more, 'yes: the wait is one day both times' for consistency, and '28' or 'all 30' for how many can be safer than the middle. Each is tested straight after and the reveal names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating scenarios (plane-crash news, revising tomorrow, scam overconfidence, joining a new team, mocked doubter in a chat, facts that don't settle a choice). Wrong answers carry tags now, group, me, vivid and known, each explaining what that bias needs ('Optimism bias is “it won’t happen to me”. Is the person rating their own risk?').

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the learner kid and adult limits. Kid text uses short sentences and concrete numbers (1 in 6, under 15 a year, 600,000). Technical terms risk, uncertainty, availability bias, present bias, optimism bias, groupthink and decision framework are defined in plain words where they first appear.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: risk vs uncertainty, availability with real numbers, present/optimism/groupthink and peers, the plan. Adult: frameworks and key terms with citations, why shortcuts fail where they do, four named mistakes, what the lab does. The filler and 12% overlap gates passed, including against Questioning Your Own Biases.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light screenshots before and after Show me on every step. Fixed after the first pass: the three bar labels in the availability step ran into each other (now two short lines each, width-capped), the result message was cut at four lines (caption now allows five), plan chips like 'Check the facts and odds' were squeezed to one tiny line (now wrapped to two), and the optimism grid labels which colour is below the line.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: 'Risk: odds known' / 'Uncertainty: odds unknown' labelled with the current card, 'Watch a shark story', one button per offer labelled 'Choice A: £10 today' etc., 'Line left' / 'Line right' / 'Check the middle', '⚑ Mia' etc. with the message in aria-label, and one button per plan step. The canvas aria-label and live region carry each message; walk.cjs ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
